public_rationale: Cloudera's September 2026 survey, released October 26, reports that 45% of respondents moved AI workloads because of higher or more volatile costs [e1](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/26/3388376/0/en/the-ai-scale-trap-why-89-of-enterprises-are-forced-to-redesign-ai-use-cases-amid-spiraling-costs.html). ETR's August 6, 2026 report says 17% of respondents whose AI spending exceeded plan paused or scaled back initiatives [e2](https://research.etr.ai/etr-data-drop/ai-demand-is-strong.-ai-budget-control-is-still-catching-up?hs_amp=true). These findings document deployment changes and responses to overruns; neither measures a broad, material fall in realized enterprise AI expenditure [e1](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/26/3388376/0/en/the-ai-scale-trap-why-89-of-enterprises-are-forced-to-redesign-ai-use-cases-amid-spiraling-costs.html) [e2](https://research.etr.ai/etr-data-drop/ai-demand-is-strong.-ai-budget-control-is-still-catching-up?hs_amp=true).
limitations: Cloudera's commissioned survey does not show whether workload moves reduced total AI spending.
ETR's evidence predates the forecast and its 17% figure concerns respondents with spending overruns.
The packet lacks comparable realized expenditure records with consistent periods, organizational boundaries and a documented accounting basis.
The evidence does not establish that AI costs exceed every other organizational cost category.
No supplied evidence meets the early-resolution rule. The forecast has no deadline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Zitron is confident AI spending gets cut because its costs are volatile, owing to the nature of LLMs, harnesses and prompts, and are much higher than anything else in an organization.

statement.excerpt: The reason I’m so confident AI gets cut is that its cost is volatile due to the nature of LLMs and harnesses and prompts and all the other bits that go into making them do something, and are so much higher than anything else in an organization.

from_speaker: due to the nature of LLMs and harnesses and prompts
so much higher than anything else in an organization
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast of broad, material enterprise AI spending reductions caused by high and variable costs.
Confidence is not a conditional antecedent.
Cuts to individual deployments are relevant but do not by themselves establish a broad reduction in total AI spending.
The comparison with everything else in an organization is retained as an unverified premise; it is not silently narrowed to software costs.
criteria.support_condition: Representative expenditure records show material enterprise AI spending reductions, and decision records attribute them to unusually high and volatile costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence decisively establishes a completed broad retrenchment whose causes exclude the stated cost mechanism. Continued growth alone does not refute an undated prediction of eventual cuts.

evidence.explanation: This concerns respondents whose spending exceeded plan and predates the forecast. It documents some retrenchment but does not measure subsequent broad expenditure cuts.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative, comparable expenditure records showing a broad, material, realized reduction in enterprise AI spending, with decision records establishing its causes. High and volatile costs causing that reduction would support the forecast; a completed broad retrenchment whose causes exclude that mechanism would contradict it under the contract. Matched organizational accounts would test the comparison with other costs.
